You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Concordia Two thousand years ago, the Roman Empire ruled the lands around the Mediterranean Sea. With peace at the borders, harmony inside the provinces, uniform law, and a common currency, the economy thrived and gave rise to mighty Roman dynasties as they expanded throughout the numerous cities. Guide one of these dynasties and send colonists to the remote realms of the Empire; develop your trade network; and appease the ancient gods for their favor — all to gain the chance to emerge victorious! Number of players: 2 - 5 Game duration: 50 mn Complexity: 3 / 5 Play Concordia and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Game flow A player’s turn consists of playing 1 card from their hand of un-played personality cards and executing the action(s) on the card. All played cards form a personal discard pile, showing only the last card played. God cards Card Action Tribune Takes back ALL cards from your personal discard and receive 1 sestertius coin for cards returned beyond three. You may also build one additional colonist for one food + one tool in Rome (Imperial and Italy maps) Architect Move colonists, total moves equals the number of colonists. May move through other colonists but not finish in the same space. After all Movement: May build houses in cities adjacent to colonists for cost based on city type paying both goods and coins with coins multiplied by the number of houses that will be in the city after the build City Type Goods Coins Brick 1 Food 1 sestertius x houses Food 1 Brick + 1 Food 2 sestertius x houses Tool 1 Brick + 1 Tool 3 sestertius x houses Wine 1 Brick + 1 Wine 4 sestertius x houses Cloth 1 Brick + 1 Cloth 5 sestertius x houses Prefect All players produce goods in the selected province. Prefect player also gets bonus good on token (two if has Prefectus Magnus) then province flips to coin side, or collect the cash bonus (total of all coins shown on previously produced locations, which are then reset). Colonist Either build a new colonists for 1 food + 1 tool, or Collect 5 coin + 1 coin per colonist of your colour. Mercator Get the specified number of coins, then you may buy or sell up to two types of goods at prices shown on the storehouse board. Diplomat Activate the top card of another player's discard pile. Senator Buy cards, at cost of goods shown in red field of card, + what is shown under card on the board. Consul Buy one card for just the cost shown in red field of card. Specialists Produce goods as directed, one per house of that good type across all locations. Other players get no production. Production tokens are ignored, Prefefectus Magnus has no effect Game End The game end is triggered after either a player purchases the last card from the display, or after any one player builds their 15th house. In either case, this player is awarded the CONCORDIA (worth 7 additional VP) card for triggering the Game End condition. Now all OTHER players execute their final turn and ALL players tally their final victory points. Scoring Score each god condition, then multiply that score by the number of cards you have of that god. God Condition VESTA The value of all goods in your storehouse (usual price as depicted) is added to your money. Then receive 1 VP per 10 sestertii, rounded down. JUPITER For each house inside a non-brick city receive 1 VP. (max. 15 VP) SATURNUS For each province with at least one of your houses receive 1 VP. (Imperium max. 12 VP, Italia max. 11 VP) MERCURIUS For each type of goods you can produce, receive 2 VP. (max. 10 VP) MARS For each of the players colonists on the game board the player receives 2 VP. (max. 12 VP) MINERVA For each city of the related city type the player receives a certain number of VP as depicted on the specialist’s card. [Rating: 1/10] Spread Sheet Victory Point Matrix the Game.   I really wonder what happened to Gerdts. Imperial is a true classic, the new ones were just euro puzzles with a rondel. And now he is here - same thing with no rondel. More or less MPS game with some leeching (yay!) and "soft blocking" (you have to pay more!). The key is building your deck of actions - it works kinda similar to Havana (having a special action to take discard back to your hand).    Graphics are hard to read and pretty generic. The game is about optimising your way through the spread sheet with some luck and randomness included as is

[Rating: 1/10] Like a loooong slog through thigh deep mud, only to arrive just as someone beats you to it. Which wouldn't be so bad if it didn't take several turns to set up for every move. Then you can try something else if you have the correct resources, or go on with your plan if you have the money to pay double. Cards cannot be counted on as by the time your turn rolls around it may be a completely new set and not ones you can afford or even use. Locations may favor the start players and that may or may not be mitigated by the "double prizes" for the last player. Almost no way to plan ahead. Given the ra

[Rating: 1/10] Nothing wrong with game. I'm sure its a splendid affair. However after watching run through and or reading reviews, absolutely no desire to play.

[Rating: 1/10] I really want to like this game, but playing it is a slooooooow form of torture. Gave it several tries, but it's first and only game I just truly dislike.  The mechanics and the game design are great, but Concordia is incredibly low on player interaction. Since I enjoy games with a lot of player interaction, this game is regrettably not for me.

[Rating: 1/10] I came here, because of all the people rating mature themed games like KD:M or Hate with a 1, just because of their mature theme. This games theme is boring!

[Rating: 1/10] only for score maximalists. cryptic scoring, no way to gauge your progression against other players. Strategies are impossible to counter.

[Rating: 1/10] The game is good and "elegant". You have to take into account various factors with each choice.  However, I just don't find what it proposes interesting or fun. I feel like I'm just "moving and placing houses". I know there's more to it and would even recommend it to certain people, but it just isn't for me.
